newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HSBC surges to new high.
newsitem.headline: HSBC surges to new high.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc rocketed to a new high on Monday, helped by optimism about interest rates which fuelled a Wall Street surge on Friday, analysts said.
The stock was up HK$5.50 at HK$203.00 in morning trade in Hong Kong after pushing through HK$200 in London on Friday.
"Generally people are more positive about the interest rate outlook," said an analyst with a Japanese brokerage, adding that British banks were generally doing well.
Bear Stearns analyst Tom Monaco said strength in sterling had also helped push up the local share price of HSBC, which owns the British bank group Midland.
Sterling was quoted at US$1.6210/20 on Monday after dipping to US$1.60 on British election day jitters.
The Dow industrials rose 94.72 points to 7,071.20 on Friday after economic data alleviated concerns on inflation.
"The share price of HSBC is still relatively cheap compared to other international banks," said Paul Lee of Vickers Ballas.
The push through HK$200 might revive talk of a stock split for HSBC, analysts said.
"It's a positive, I guess, for retail players but the institutional guys would sell it off," said Monaco, who plans to formally initiate coverage of the bank on May 7.
